Subject: Request: SIG + short architecture overview for Dedicated/Private

Hi Kimberly,

We're running Sable's SIG intake for our platform adoption and have a few follow-ups specific to Redwood's Dedicated and Private deployment isolation models. The SIG spreadsheet is attached — we flagged the network/isolation questions. Two asks we hope you can cover in a short deliverable:

- A concise architecture overview (one page narrative) that explains control-plane vs data-plane separation for both Dedicated and Private.
- Two diagrams: (a) control-plane vs data-plane annotated diagram and (b) tenant-fencing/egress demarcation for private deployments (showing guardrails, KMS boundary, and any airlock/egress proxies).

Can you confirm you can provide these artifacts by EOD Tuesday, Apr 27? If you need a shorter list, we can prioritize the diagram + a CAIQ mapping for the relevant SIG rows.

Thanks — attaching the SIG export (SIG-questionnaire.xlsx) and our intake sheet.

Lina Park

1) Ben — do you need SLA/latency numbers included in the diagram (they sometimes want expected p99s to understand buffering and caching placement)?
2) Jordan — do we have an updated control-plane diagram (last year we used the sentinel partitioning sketch). If not, Ben and I can annotate and produce a simplified variant for the auditor.

I'll assemble a zip and a Drive link for Lina. If timeline is tight, we'll push only the diagram + CAIQ mapping first and narrative as an addendum.

-Kim

Cc: procurement@sableanalytics.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-27T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Deliver: control/data-plane diagram + tenant-fencing package (SIG rows mapped)

Hi Lina — thanks for the patience. Attached are the artifacts Sable requested:

1) controlplane_vs_dataplane-diagram.pdf — annotated diagram showing control-plane partitioning (auth, orchestration, and management APIs) vs data-plane (inference runtime, KV cache, and model serving paths). The diagram highlights the separation model we apply in Dedicated and how it changes for Private (customer-managed control-plane vs Redwood-managed control signals).

2) tenant-fencing-annotated.pdf — tenant fencing map for Private deployments showing egress demarcation, KMS boundary, and the optional airlock/proxy pattern we recommend when customers require strict egress vetting. Margin notes include short mitigations for lateral movement scenarios.

3) CAIQ-responses.xlsx — a CAIQ-aligned mapping for the SIG rows you flagged. Column "Redwood answer" provides the short answer and a reference to the diagram (page/figure) where appropriate.

Summary (one-paragraph): Redwood enforces tenant separation using strict network ACLs, workload identity for control-plane actions, and cryptographic isolation for customer keys. In Dedicated we operate dedicated GPU pools with explicit VLAN segmentation and per-tenant routing; in Private we provide configuration templates and a hardened airlock/egress proxy pattern customers can deploy to enforce outbound controls. Shared services (metrics, billing) are logically separated with least-privilege service accounts and are accessible only through a service-mesh ingress with enforced mTLS.

Next steps: If you'd like, we can carve out a 30-minute walkthrough next week to walk Sable's reviewers through the diagrams. Proposed slots: Tue Apr 30 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed May 1 11:00–11:30 PT. Please let me know which works.

Artifacts are delivered as attachments and uploaded to a Drive folder (link below).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1FAKEDIAGRAM

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
